editorial_note: Five fresh picks from the official all-language daily GitHub Trending listing: specialist Android guidance, test-first agent workflows, document-focused career tooling, agent operations and a non-AI cloud-file utility. Curation order reflects practical interest, not GitHub rank. Trending is not a release date or an endorsement.
coverage_notes: All 13 listing entries were inspected. Exact primary public GitHub metadata, README and license endpoints were checked for all six non-repeat candidates; all six were active and unarchived. Five were selected. Seven entries already featured on 15-16 October were omitted without claiming a material update.

Cursor plugins was not selected: it overlaps the previously featured plugin-directory theme, and although its README says MIT, the repository API detects no license and the root license endpoint returns 404. This is a licensing-verification limitation, not a finding that the project is unsafe.

The preceding seven calendar dates, 10-16 October, were checked for local history. The archive began on 15 October, so only two prior editions exist; 10-14 October have no local issues. None of today's picks repeats the available history.

The official listing was captured at 08:00:36 Europe/Paris. Literal stars-today labels are GitHub's displayed period figures; API total stars and README evidence were checked separately at the times shown per card. They are not an independently audited rolling-24-hour growth measurement.

This remains an AI-heavy source snapshot. There is no fresh dedicated security-tool pick: agent permission boundaries and configuration review provide today's defensive-security angle. LinkSwift supplies the non-AI selection, not a claim of balanced coverage across software.

Capabilities, performance, adoption and security guarantees are maintainer descriptions unless expressly identified otherwise. No candidate code, installers, plugins, models, browser sessions or credentials were used. Stars and ranking are not a security audit or endorsement; no human review was performed.

projects.description: Modular instructions and resources for coding agents working on Android, grounded in Android developer guidance and distributed in the Agent Skills format.
projects.why_interesting: A focused alternative to generic coding advice: the maintainers say they prioritize workflows where their evaluations find models underperform, rather than basic Compose tips. The README illustrates specialist R8 analysis and edge-to-edge UI tasks.
projects.caveat: These are instructions, not a correctness guarantee: the README explicitly requires checking AI results. Skill installation can target every detected agent, so review scope and contents first. Public contributions are not currently accepted; no Android build or model evaluation was run.

projects.description: A composable development workflow for coding agents, linking design approval, implementation plans, isolated worktrees, test-driven development and code review.
projects.why_interesting: Useful when the failure mode is an agent rushing into implementation: it makes design, failing-test evidence and review explicit stages. The README documents both task-by-task subagents and a cheaper single-context execution path.
projects.caveat: Mandatory workflow instructions can add latency and token cost, and installation is harness-specific. The optional visual companion loads a version-bearing remote logo by default; the README documents telemetry opt-outs. Process guidance does not prove generated code is correct, and no plugin was installed.

projects.description: A local-file job-application workflow built around Claude Code, with posting evaluation, tailored CV and cover-letter drafting, PDF checks, interview preparation and an application tracker.
projects.why_interesting: The practical distinction is document verification: the README describes compiling PDFs, checking extracted text for applicant-tracking readability and using a separate reviewer, rather than stopping at generated prose. It also documents an offline HTML tracking dashboard.
projects.caveat: The README warns that setup writes personal information into tracked files: use a private working repository, not a public fork, for real applications. Model access and the document toolchain add cost and setup. Several portal integrations are Denmark-focused, and the README says automated LinkedIn access conflicts with its terms. Review every factual claim before submitting; no applications or personal data were processed.

projects.description: An agent coordination layer for Claude Code and Codex, with CLI/MCP tools, persistent memory, workflow monitoring and a plugin-based console.
projects.why_interesting: Worth inspecting for multi-agent operations: the README distinguishes lightweight plugin use from a fuller setup with hooks and a daemon, and separates recorded console actions from proof that underlying swarm work completed. Its configuration-review tooling is a defensive security lead, not evidence of a security audit.
projects.caveat: The README says runtime mods execute with the user account permissions and are not sandboxed. Full setup changes agent configuration and can enable background activity; capability support varies by client. Performance, learning and security guarantees remain maintainer claims. No hooks, MCP servers or daemons were enabled.

projects.description: A JavaScript userscript that obtains download URLs from supported cloud-drive services and connects them to downloader workflows, with browser-interface adjustments.
projects.why_interesting: The non-AI utility in this snapshot: potentially useful when an authorized cloud-drive download needs to work without the official desktop client. Its README explicitly separates obtaining links through service APIs from unsupported speed-limit-bypass claims.
projects.caveat: Review userscript permissions, update sources and handling of account tokens or session data before any use. Provider API changes and service terms can break workflows; obtaining a URL does not grant redistribution rights or bypass entitlements. The API-selected default branch is dev, and its README labels the canary unstable. AGPL-3.0 obligations apply; no script, account session or file download was accessed.
